title: Move Fast and Don't Break Things: Scaling Databases for the AI Era — PlanetScale
talk_summary: A PlanetScale infrastructure talk arguing that reliability principles (isolation, redundancy, sharding, back pressure, decoupling) should be applied from day one, and that exposing complex infra through simple text/JSON config files, CLIs, and MCP servers makes it safely operable by AI agents. The agent-specific content is thin: it mostly argues that git-like branching/deploy-request/revert primitives for databases are also good primitives for agents.

takeaways.technique: Back pressure with graceful degradation instead of hard failure
takeaways.what_they_do: Tag/categorize incoming traffic and set resource budgets per segment; when a segment exceeds its budget, warn the client, throttle, and if needed kill those queries so the rest of the system stays healthy rather than crashing entirely.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's much better than your whole application going down and being offline for all of your users

takeaways.technique: Failure isolation between control plane and data plane
takeaways.what_they_do: Design so that a bad deploy to the control plane (or observability/analytics/MCP components) cannot take down the data plane or block access to critical state.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if I deploy a bad ship to the control plane and take it down, nothing else is impacted

takeaways.technique: Expose complex infra as simple declarative config + CLI/MCP for agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Hide complex sharding behind a simple JSON vschema file, and expose operations via CLI and MCP server so agents can read/modify config and trigger deploys safely.
takeaways.evidence_quote: AI agents are excellent at working with things like text files and JSON files

takeaways.technique: Branch + deploy-request + one-click revert for stateful changes
takeaways.what_they_do: Mirror the git flow for database schema: branch schema in isolation, merge via deploy request with no downtime, and one-click revert without data loss; expose via API/CLI so agents can automate it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you deploy a schema change and you see a problem, we give you the ability to oneclick revert
